chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be killed due to it, belittled, and I do not think killing him would be an expiation for him, and he would not inherit her'.

key_terms.صَاغِراً: Belittled or humiliated (referring to the manner of execution)
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ بِهَا: He is executed due to it (referring to the mother's blood money/diyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a son who kills his mother regarding execution, inheritance, and expiation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that a son who kills his mother is executed specifically for her blood money (diyah) but is not considered to have expiated his sin through his own death, nor does he inherit from her. This ruling underscores the unique gravity of filicide in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the legal penalty of execution from spiritual expiation, a view supported by the principle that killing a parent constitutes a major sin (dhanb kabir) requiring more than mere retribution.
